personal_item_dimensions.notes: Ryanair lists the same three dimensions in different axis orders — 40 x 30 x 20 cm on the Bag Policy page, 40x20x30cm on the fare bundles page. The maximum bag is the same either way, so the order is presentational. Stated here in the Bag Policy page's order as the more authoritative source.

priority_cabin_bag_dimensions.notes: Stated identically on both pages: 'a 10kg bag (55x40x20cm) onboard, to be stored in the overhead locker' and '1 10kg Cabin Bag (55x40x20cm)'. Requires Priority boarding; it is not included in the Basic fare.

priority_cabin_bag_weight.notes: The draft flagged 10kg as ambiguous against a checked tier of the same weight. Resolved: the checked one is 'a 10kg Check-in Bag' dropped at the desk, this is 'a second 10kg cabin bag' in the overhead locker. Different products.

infant_allowance.value: No cabin allowance; 5 kg baby bag plus two baby equipment items, free
infant_allowance.notes: Verbatim: 'Infants have no cabin allowance but may bring a 5kg baby bag and two baby equipment items free.' The count of two was written as a word, so the extractor missed it — captured by hand from the source.

included_checked_allowance.value: None — no checked bag is included in any fare
included_checked_allowance.notes: Every tier is described as an addition: 'you can add a 10kg Check-in Bag to your booking'. No fare includes checked baggage.

purchasable_tiers.value: 10 kg · 20 kg (up to 3 per booking) · 23 kg (up to 1 per booking)
purchasable_tiers.notes: Verbatim: '20kg Check-in Bag… Passengers can purchase up to 3 checked bags of 20kg on their booking. 23kg Check-in Bag… up to 1 checked bags of 23kg.' No per-booking limit is stated for the 10kg tier.

excess_fees.notes: No source. The baggage_fees URL is a help-centre category index, not an article — captured at 748 chars, below the threshold. Needs a real fees article URL.

basic_fare.value: 1 small cabin bag under the seat. No checked baggage. Randomly assigned seat.
basic_fare.notes: Verbatim: 'It's our cheapest fare and includes 1 Small Cabin Bag (40x20x30cm), which must fit under the seat in front of you, with no additional baggage allowance… your seat will be randomly assigned.'

regular_fare.value: Standard seat, Priority boarding, 2 cabin bags — 1 small under the seat plus 1 × 10 kg in the locker

plus_fare.value: Standard seat, 1 small cabin bag, 1 × 20 kg checked bag
plus_fare.notes: Also lists free airport check-in, but only for bookings made before 14 August 2025 — a closed cohort, so it is not part of what the fare includes today.

family_plus_fare.value: 1 small cabin bag, 1 × 10 kg checked bag per group member, 1 × 20 kg family checked bag, free seats for under-12s. Bookings of up to six with at least one child or teen.

flexi_plus_fare.value: Priority boarding, 2 cabin bags, reserved seating, Fast Track where available, flight changes

conditions_of_carriage_url.notes: The FR-operated terms. Ryanair UK (RK), Buzz (RR) and Malta Air publish separate documents — see contracting_parties in the rights module.

online_checkin_window.notes: Stated on the fare bundles page under Basic Fare, not on a check-in page — the check-in URL in carriers.json is a help-centre category index and captured too short to extract from.

airport_bag_drop_cutoff.notes: No candidates — same category-index problem as online_checkin_window.

modules.title: If your flight is delayed or cancelled

contracting_parties.value: Four operators under separate terms: Ryanair (FR), Ryanair UK (RK), Ryanair Sun/Buzz (RR), Malta Air. Which applies depends on the operating code of your flight.
contracting_parties.notes: The page we captured is a disambiguation page, not the terms themselves. Each operator links to its own General Terms & Conditions of Carriage.

governing_regime.notes: Not sourced, and cannot be a single value — see contracting_parties. Four documents govern four operators. EU261 and UK261 apply by departure point regardless, but that is reasoning rather than a source.

conditions_of_carriage_url.notes: The terms governing FR-operated flights. Ryanair UK (RK), Buzz (RR) and Malta Air publish separate documents — see contracting_parties in the rights module. The source is the disambiguation page that links here, which is where the URL was read, not the document itself.
